chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Is’haq Bin Ammar, from Abu Al Hassan Musa (peace be upon him)
Regarding the surfaces in which there is Mention of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, he said: ‘Wash it’.

key_terms.اغْسِلْهَا: Wash it (imperative verb for ritual washing)
key_terms.الظُّهُور: Surfaces or skins (often referring to parchment or paper)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on washing surfaces that have the name of Allah written on them?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS) clarifies the status of surfaces inscribed with the Divine Name, ruling that they are subject to standard ritual washing (ghusl) rather than requiring unique preservation methods like burning. It highlights the Shia scholarly view that the sanctity of the Name does not preclude the object from undergoing normal purification processes to remove minor impurities, distinguishing it from the specific rulings on burning written Quranic verses.
